title: Map the cosmic dark ages and first luminous structures in three dimensions

concept.text: The innovation is validated three-dimensional mapping of the early Universe through the redshifted 21-cm signal from neutral hydrogen. Observations would recover spatial variations in 21-cm brightness temperature across the sky and across redshift, revealing how structure changed over cosmic time. The goal is to resolve an evolving cosmic volume, extending beyond a sky-averaged measurement or a statistical estimate of fluctuations.

Brightness temperature is the observable; a map does not directly identify every gas property or luminous object. Its interpretation depends on physical modelling of gas conditions and radiation backgrounds. During cosmic dawn and reionisation, those conditions carry the collective imprint of the first luminous sources. The concept also encompasses the earlier dark ages, but the supplied evidence directly grounds the mapping case for cosmic dawn and reionisation and does not establish comparable observational reach into the earlier era.

significance.text: Successful spatial recovery across redshift would make a poorly observed period accessible as an evolving three-dimensional volume. Researchers could examine where early structure developed and how radiation from emerging sources affected surrounding hydrogen. The revolutionary advance would be access to the spatial organisation and evolution of that field, beyond detecting its average behaviour or measuring the aggregate strength of fluctuations.

Interpreted through physical models, such maps could constrain early gas conditions and the populations responsible for the radiation signatures. Their scientific value would depend on which spatial scales and redshifts were recovered reliably. Observing a brightness-temperature pattern would not by itself uniquely determine the properties of its sources, and extending the impact claim from cosmic dawn to the earlier dark ages requires additional evidence about achievable coverage.

Conceptual synthesis: this would provide environmental context for discoveries of the first stars and early massive black holes. Combining a mapped hydrogen environment with independently identified objects could help test explanations of their influence. Those downstream possibilities depend on suitable overlapping observations and successful interpretation; a hydrogen map alone would not establish the identity of individual first-generation stars or resolve how the earliest black holes formed.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable recovery of the cosmological 21-cm brightness-temperature field as spatially resolved maps over multiple redshift intervals. A statistical upper limit constrains how large fluctuations could be without recovering their locations. A sky-averaged measurement follows the mean signal with redshift without locating structure across the sky. Tomography requires enough sensitivity and control of contamination to retain spatial information as well as spectral information.

The cosmological signal is faint relative to foreground radio emission. Radio-frequency interference, ionospheric scintillation and instrumental calibration errors further complicate its recovery. The engineering challenge includes collecting sufficiently sensitive observations and calibrating the instrument accurately enough that contamination does not masquerade as cosmological structure. The analysis must also distinguish foreground removal from inadvertent removal or distortion of the desired signal.

A further unresolved step is demonstrating that validation methods support map recovery. The reviewed NenuFAR study injected simulated signals before foreground removal to assess bias in recovered power spectra within specified signal families. That is useful evidence about the analysis pipeline, but it does not establish faithful recovery of a three-dimensional cosmological image. Map-level fidelity, robustness to different plausible signals and coverage of the earlier dark ages remain additional requirements.

current_state.text: Munshi and colleagues reported in 2025 that four nights of NenuFAR observations yielded upper limits on cosmic-dawn 21-cm fluctuations in bins centred at redshifts 17.0 and 20.3. The abstract describes power-spectrum upper limits, and the supplied full-text review records an explicit non-detection of the cosmological signal. This result therefore demonstrates an upper-limit measurement at those redshifts, not a recovered three-dimensional cosmological map.

The arXiv landing page lists a 2025 journal reference associated with DOI 10.1093/mnras/staf1386. The supplied review distinguishes that bibliographic information from preprint and placeholder acceptance information in the PDF. It also distinguishes foreground images and intermediate data cubes from cosmological tomography: producing those analysis products does not establish detection or mapping of the underlying cosmological field.

The reviewed paper describes tomographic mapping as a prospective capability associated with increased sensitivity, including discussion of the upcoming SKA. Such prospects are projections rather than demonstrated maps. The supplied review draws on both an abstract-bearing landing page and a complete 23-page text extraction, so the assessment is not restricted to abstract access. However, the supplied freshness record is empty: it does not establish the latest field-wide state through 2026-11-01 or assess subsequent achievements. That gap limits claims about present-day progress; it is not evidence that later results do not exist.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independently calibrated observations should recover consistent spatial maps of cosmological 21-cm brightness temperature across multiple redshift intervals. The recovered field should resolve evolving structure over a volume large enough to support the stated scientific conclusions. Before assessing success, investigators would need to specify the required volume, spatial resolution, redshift coverage, uncertainty and observing effort. These are proposed criteria; the supplied evidence does not establish numerical thresholds or a consensus completion standard.
completion_criteria.label: Independently calibrated 21-cm maps consistently resolve structure across multiple redshifts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: realistic signal-injection tests should quantify how calibration and foreground treatment alter recovered structure, including signal loss, bias and false features. The NenuFAR paper provides a methodological basis through injections used to assess power-spectrum recovery, but convincing tomography would require extending validation to the maps themselves. Testing should cover several plausible signal structures rather than demonstrating recovery only for a narrow simulated family.
completion_criteria.label: Map-level signal injections quantify recovery distortions across plausible signal structures

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent reductions and, where feasible, independent observations should reproduce the main structures within stated uncertainties. Comparisons with independent tracers should be used where suitable observations exist. Results should disclose the scales and redshifts that remain inaccessible, the sensitivity of conclusions to physical modelling and the observing resources required. A demonstration confined to cosmic dawn or reionisation should be described at that scope; earlier dark-ages coverage requires its own evidence. Finite tests would establish demonstrated breadth and reliability within those boundaries, not universal recovery under every possible condition.
completion_criteria.label: Independent reductions reproduce structures within stated uncertainties and disclosed limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: AST-11, “Identify the first generation of metal-free stars,” has the closest direct overlap. AST-06 concerns the spatial hydrogen field and the collective effects of early radiation sources; AST-11 concerns identifying a particular stellar population. A mapped radiation imprint would not alone identify individual metal-free stars, while identifying those stars would not itself produce volumetric hydrogen maps. Only the AST-11 title is supplied, so its detailed requirements and precise overlap remain unassessed.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-13, “Establish how the earliest massive black holes formed and grew,” shares the early-source setting. Hydrogen tomography could potentially provide environmental and radiation context relevant to explanations of early black-hole growth. Establishing their formation and growth history would require additional evidence connecting those environments to the black holes themselves; neither concept completes the other.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-05, “Detect and identify a primordial gravitational-wave background,” and AST-12, “Directly detect the cosmic neutrino background,” also seek observational access to cosmic history through different signals. Their overlap with AST-06 is the broader ambition of opening difficult observational windows. Their observables and completion requirements remain distinct from mapping the high-redshift hydrogen brightness-temperature field.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-08, “Produce resolved surface maps of rocky exoplanets,” shares the requirement to demonstrate reliable spatial reconstruction. Its target is a planetary surface, whereas AST-06 seeks an evolving cosmological volume. AST-03 and AST-04, concerning the constituent of dark matter and the cause of cosmic acceleration, could potentially benefit from additional cosmological observations, but successful 21-cm tomography would not by itself establish either physical explanation.

brief.title: A map of the Universe before and around its first stars
possible: Astronomers could explore a three-dimensional map of the Universe before and during the rise of its first stars. They would follow how structure changed over time using the 21-cm signal, a radio signal from hydrogen gas, and locate the patterns left by the earliest sources of light.
why: Researchers could study where early structure developed and how emerging sources of light affected surrounding gas. The maps would give discoveries of early stars and black holes a wider environmental context and help test explanations of their influence.

sources.showed: NenuFAR observations set tighter limits on how strongly the hydrogen radio signal could vary across space during the first stars' era. The team did not detect the cosmological signal.
sources.quote:
yielding a 50-fold reduction
in the excess variance compared to a previous analysis of the north celestial pole field.
sources.cited_for: The work demonstrates improved control of contamination and tighter limits on early hydrogen signal variations.
sources.not_established: Limits on signal variations do not recover their locations or establish a three-dimensional map.

sources.showed: Tests with simulated signals showed that adjusting how the LOFAR radio telescope's response is corrected can avoid erasing faint signals, but can also increase noise.
sources.quote:
We show that suppression of faint signals can eﬀectively be avoided
by calibrating these short baselines using only the longer baselines.
sources.cited_for: Instrument corrections must preserve the faint signal while controlling added noise.
sources.not_established: The tests do not demonstrate faithful recovery of spatial maps across varied plausible hydrogen patterns.

sources.showed: HERA's upgraded instrument set limits on hydrogen signal variations during the first stars' era and afterward. Unwanted foreground radio emission still contaminated part of the measurement.
sources.quote:
mutual coupling has become our dominant systematic, leaking foreground power that strongly contaminates the
low-k modes
sources.cited_for: The upgraded instrument extends statistical constraints while exposing contamination that limits recovery.
sources.not_established: These statistical limits do not establish spatially resolved maps of the early hydrogen signal.

sources.showed: HERA's first observing phase tightened limits on hydrogen signal variations. With physical models, the team ruled out a broad set of scenarios in which the gas stayed cold.
sources.quote:
we ﬁnd that
the intergalactic medium must have been heated above the adiabatic cooling limit at least as early as
z = 10.4
sources.cited_for: Statistical limits already constrain explanations of early gas heating.
sources.not_established: Model-based constraints on gas heating do not locate the heated regions in a map.

shown: Munshi and colleagues using NenuFAR, and the HERA Collaboration, have set upper limits: ceilings on how strong spatial variations in the hydrogen signal could be. These measurements constrain early-Universe models but have not recovered the locations of cosmic structures.
missing: Reliable maps must recover the hydrogen signal across the sky and through successive periods despite much brighter radio contamination.
Tests must establish how instrument corrections and contamination removal erase, distort or invent mapped structures.
Independent analyses must reproduce the mapped structures within stated uncertainties.

milestones.label: Independently calibrated maps resolve evolving structure
milestones.explanation: Observations with independently corrected instrument responses would have to recover consistent maps across successive periods, with stated coverage and precision. This would establish recovery of an evolving cosmic volume.

milestones.label: Simulated signals reveal distortions in recovered maps
milestones.explanation: Tests adding varied realistic signals would have to measure lost structure, bias and false features in the recovered maps. This would establish how faithfully the analysis preserves cosmic patterns.

milestones.label: Independent analyses reproduce structures within stated limits
milestones.explanation: Independent analyses and, where feasible, observations would have to reproduce structures within stated uncertainties. Disclosed coverage, model dependence and observing effort would define the demonstrated reach.

uncertain: The sensitivity and instrument performance needed to reach the dark ages before the first stars remain unresolved.
The required mapped volume, detail, time coverage, precision and observing effort have no agreed thresholds.
Different gas conditions and source populations may produce similar patterns, limiting how uniquely maps can explain the first luminous sources.

page.title: 21-cm tomography of cosmic dawn and reionisation
page.definition: Three-dimensional images recover fluctuations in neutral hydrogen’s redshifted 21-cm radio brightness during the formation of the first luminous sources and the ionisation of intergalactic gas. Sky position supplies two dimensions; observing frequency supplies redshift, and hence distance and lookback time.

goal.need: Foreground radio emission is approximately 100,000–1,000,000 times brighter than the cosmological signal. Hydrogen fluctuations record heating and ionisation by the first stars and black holes. A power spectrum measures fluctuation strength but does not determine spatial arrangement: the SKA science book demonstrates different simulated images with identical power spectra. Tomography supplies the locations and shapes that this statistic loses.

statements.body: SKAO Epoch of Reionisation/Cosmic Dawn Science Working Group
statements.quote: The original baseline design for SKA-Low was motivated by the ability to produce tomographic images of the redshifted 21-cm signal

completion.title: Cosmological 21-cm image cubes meet the SKA deep-survey target of approximately 1 mK image noise.
completion.criterion: Directly image ionised structures and neutral-hydrogen brightness-temperature fluctuations over redshifts z = 6–28, on redshift-dependent angular scales of 5–300 arcminutes, at approximately 1 mK rms brightness-temperature sensitivity. The published deep-survey reference covers five separate 20-square-degree fields, totalling 100 square degrees, with 1000 hours per field and 0.1 MHz science-frequency sampling. Calibration and foreground subtraction must satisfy the source’s assumption that thermal noise dominates the image error budget. Adjacent frequency images form the cosmological image cubes.
completion.set_by: SKA Organisation CD/EoR Science Working Group, 2015 Science Book, Sections 5, 6.1 and 6.2.
completion.basis: The working group explicitly publishes this as the deep survey’s direct-imaging science goal. It specifies spatial structure, sensitivity, angular scales, redshift coverage and survey area. This is a historical science target, not a certification standard. The 2026 observing plan places statistical measurements over 5.5 < z < 27 but describes tomography as available below z = 10; it does not establish achievement of the broader target.

milestones.title: An interferometer simulation recovers injected 21-cm power without unaccounted signal loss.
milestones.criterion: Recover the input power spectrum of a boosted Gaussian 21-cm analogue after the published HERA end-to-end simulation includes foregrounds, thermal noise, calibration errors and instrumental systematics. After the specified signal-loss corrections, there must be no evidence of additional suppression. HERA’s 2023 analysis demonstrated this recovery in simulations matching 94 observing nights, across two frequency bands and five sky fields.
milestones.set_by: HERA Collaboration, published end-to-end recovery experiment, Section IV.2 and Figure 14.
milestones.threshold_quote: there is no evidence for an additional, unaccounted-for contribution to signal loss

milestones.title: 21-cm observations exclude unheated gas models at z = 10.4 with more than 95% posterior credibility.
milestones.criterion: Apply HERA’s four-model inference test: at z = 10.4, more than 95% of each model’s posterior requires gas heated above the adiabatic cooling limit. HERA Phase I met this model-dependent test using 94 nights. NenuFAR’s four-night analysis at z = 17.0 and 20.3 reported upper limits. HERA Phase II’s 14-night analysis reported limits of 1.13 × 10^6 mK² at z = 16.78, k = 0.55 h Mpc⁻¹, and 1.78 × 10^3 mK² at z = 7.05, k = 0.70 h Mpc⁻¹. Here h is the Hubble constant divided by 100 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹.
milestones.set_by: HERA Collaboration’s published 95% posterior-credibility convention, Section VII and Figure 27; conclusions depend on each model and its priors.
milestones.threshold_quote: above the adiabatic cooling limit at $>$95% credibility.

milestones.title: An observed cosmological 21-cm power-spectrum band is detected at at least 5σ.
milestones.criterion: Measure a cosmological 21-cm power-spectrum bandpower at least five times its standard error. Use the published covariance treatment including thermal noise and non-Gaussian cosmic variance. The cited sensitivity study applies this 5σ convention to reionisation, including foreground-avoidance cases; its calculations are not observational detections. The SKA imaging chapter submitted on 23 June 2026 states that no precursor interferometer had achieved a detection.
milestones.set_by: The 5σ detectability convention used by Shaw, Bharadwaj and Mondal, Sections 4–5; published application concerns reionisation.

milestones.title: 21-cm images recover ionised regions and cosmic-dawn structure at 10 mK image noise.
milestones.criterion: Recover spatial structure at the SKA working group’s published 10 mK rms imaging targets: ionised-region shapes at approximately 4 arcminutes at z ≈ 9, and cosmic-dawn spin-temperature structure at approximately 6 arcminutes at z ≈ 16 and 14 arcminutes at z ≈ 25. The reference calculation uses 1000 hours and frequency bandwidth matched to angular resolution. These are published sensitivity targets; the examples in the source are simulations.
milestones.set_by: SKA CD/EoR Science Working Group, Mellema and colleagues’ 2015 tomography chapter, Section 3.

not_found: No universally adopted numerical acceptance threshold for cosmological map fidelity or independent map replication was located in the SKA requirements and science-book documents.
No corresponding completion test for tomography of the pre-stellar dark ages at z > 30 was located in those documents.
